heading: Monday, July 20, 2026
topLine: 2 stories on AI and open problems: Jacobian conjecture counterexample and Buzzard: 'outcounterexampled'.

items.headline: Claude-assisted counterexample refutes the Jacobian conjecture in three dimensions
items.summary: Levent Alpöge (Anthropic) posted an explicit degree-7 polynomial map from C³ to C³, found with Claude Fable 5. The map has constant Jacobian determinant −2 but sends three distinct points to the same output, which disproves Keller's 1939 conjecture in every dimension of 3 or more. Alpöge credited Akhil Mathew with prompting the question. Terence Tao published an exposition of the map, and an Archive of Formal Proofs entry checks the key identities in Isabelle/HOL. The two-variable case remains open, and there is no peer-reviewed paper.

items.headline: Kevin Buzzard: AI counterexamples plus Lean make conjectures checkable
items.summary: Buzzard surveyed recent AI-found counterexamples, including to Erdős's unit distance conjecture, a Grothendieck question on finite flat group schemes, and the Jacobian conjecture. He said he does not read AI-generated informal mathematics but checks Lean statements and proofs instead. He argued that the next task for humans is understanding what the counterexamples reveal.
